prompt: Three instances of a job scheduler run for redundancy, but only one may trigger the nightly billing run, or customers get billed twice.
why: Elect a leader (ZooKeeper, etcd, Raft); only the leader schedules, and another takes over if it dies.
trap: Idempotency makes a duplicate run harmless, but you still want exactly one scheduler doing the work.

prompt: During a network partition, both database nodes believed they were primary and accepted conflicting writes.
tells: both database nodes believed they were primary
why: A quorum-based election means only the side with a majority can have a leader, so split brain can't happen.
trap: You already had replicas; the missing piece is agreement on who leads.

prompt: Workers on many machines must never process the same customer's ledger at the same time.
tells: never process the same customer's ledger at the same time
why: A lock (with a lease and fencing token) held through a consensus store like etcd.
trap: Rate limiting slows workers down; it doesn't make them mutually exclusive.

prompt: Every node in a cluster must agree on the current membership list, even when some nodes crash mid-update.
why: A consensus protocol (Raft, Paxos) commits each change only once a majority accepts it.
trap: Consistent hashing uses the membership list; it doesn't make nodes agree on it.
